# `docs/` — command reference

* **Status:** Generated. Do not edit by hand.
* **Generated by:** `uv run tools/docs/commands.py`
* **Guard:** `uv run tools/docs/commands.py --check` (from a workstation with `uv` and `docker`) and `tools/docs/check-commands.sh` (inside the build container, wired into `tools/test-all.sh`) both fail if this is stale.

---

## What this is, and where each entry comes from

**Every binary below is run as `<name> --help` inside the build container** (`tools/container/exec.sh`), against whatever `cargo build --workspace --bins` produced there. The text after each heading is copied verbatim — stdout and stderr interleaved exactly as the binary wrote them, nothing added and nothing summarised.

**15 of 22 binaries are generated here.** The rest have no usable `--help` surface off a running machine or off this project's own build — see the table at the foot of this document for which, and why. `tools/docs/commands-manifest.tsv` is the list both this generator and the in-container check read, so the two cannot name different binaries.

---

## Host-side binaries

Installed onto a workstation — `cargo install --path cmd/<name> --force --locked` from this repository's root, once per binary, per `AGENTS.md` §10. **`cargo-rivet` and `rivet-provision` are installed together**: `cargo rivet provision` runs the second one as its interview, needs no source checkout once it is there, and refuses a pair whose builds disagree (`.rulings/` R-191, R-192).

### `cargo-rivet`

```
cargo-rivet 0.1.137 (<commit>)

usage: cargo rivet setup            [--at DIR] [--name NAME] [--check]
       cargo rivet doctor           [--for run|app|image]...
       cargo rivet package          [options]
       cargo rivet library          --name N --version V --object PATH [options]
       cargo rivet bump             [PATH]
       cargo rivet update           [options]
       cargo rivet install          --host HOST [--rvt F.rvt | --artifact ID] [--enable] [confirm]
       cargo rivet deploy           (interactive — no arguments; an agent uses `install`)
       cargo rivet fleet            init|publish|list|plan|drift|push|sync|record|objects|phones|retire|hide|unhide [--at DIR] [options]
       cargo rivet artifacts        (interactive — no arguments; an agent uses `fleet retire|hide|unhide`)
       cargo rivet image            [--img PATH] --version V --arch TOKEN [options]
       cargo rivet write-image      [--image PATH] [--document PATH] [--device PATH]
       cargo rivet provision        preflight, image selection, the interview, an enrollment check, then write-image and recording [--image PATH-OR-DIGEST] [--platform TOKEN] [--device PATH] [--document PATH | --existing HOSTNAME] [--staging PATH] [--identity PATH | --pin HEX] [confirm]
       cargo rivet run              --host HOST:PORT --identity DIR --pin HEX -- <rivet command>
       cargo rivet screenshot       --host HOST:PORT --identity DIR --pin HEX [--path P | --holder] [--out F.png] [--json]
       cargo rivet secrets          [DEVICE] APPLICATION [--host HOST:PORT --identity DIR --pin HEX] [--name N] [confirm]
       cargo rivet backup           --host HOST:PORT --identity DIR --pin HEX --into DIR [--service NAME]... [confirm]
       cargo rivet restore          --host HOST:PORT --identity DIR --pin HEX --service NAME --from FILE [confirm]
       cargo rivet backup-secrets   --host HOST:PORT --identity DIR --pin HEX --into DIR [confirm]
       cargo rivet restore-secrets  --host HOST:PORT --identity DIR --pin HEX --from DIR [--replace] [confirm]
       cargo rivet recover          HOSTNAME --from DIR [--secrets DIR] [--at DIR] [--after-boot] [--replace APP]... [confirm]
       cargo rivet inspect          FILE.rvt --trusted-key PATH [--extract-program PATH]
       cargo rivet armada           list|add|forget|set-backup-dir|set-keep
       cargo rivet identity         new --directory DIR
       cargo rivet key              SEED [--out PATH] | backup DIR | restore DIR [--replace]

WHICH `cargo-rivet` IS THIS? The line above is this build's version and the
commit it came from. If a `cargo rivet` you ran printed NO version line, or
refused `--version`, or told you `deploy` SENDS A PAYLOAD OVER A LOGIN SESSION,
you are talking to an old binary on your PATH and not to this repository's
build: there is one transport here, and the current tool has `run`, which
speaks ADR-035's control plane. Install this one over it with
  cargo install --path cmd/cargo-rivet --force --locked
  cargo install --path cmd/rivet-provision --force --locked
from the repository root, or invoke the built binary by path. BOTH lines are
the install: `provision` runs rivet-provision as its interview, and the two
builds have to match. There is no self-update: `cargo rivet update` builds a
SYSTEM UPDATE payload for a board and does nothing to this tool.

`package` emits an APPLICATION .rvt from a Rust crate; `update` emits a
SYSTEM UPDATE .rvt from a built system image; `install` builds one, sends
it to a board over ADR-035's control plane and installs it. `deploy`
(bare — no arguments) is the interactive interview that composes
`install`, `secrets` and `run` for you; a script or an agent wants
`install` instead. ONE PLANNER DRIVES BOTH: `install` waits for its own
install to finish and then prints the steps that remain, as the exact
commands the interview would have run.

`bump` increments a standalone application's PATCH version (the Z of
X.Y.Z, never the minor or major) and commits it alone — the deliberate
pre-package step tools/card/bump.sh already is for the system image
(ADR-027 §10.2): refuse a dirty tree, bump the patch, commit "Version
X.Y.Z", so version and commit stay a 1:1 mapping. It refuses a version
written `version.workspace = true` (inherited from a workspace root —
for a cmd/* OS binary that number is bump.sh's). `package` and `library`
stay pure reads; a LIBRARY has no versioned source, so it is out of
scope. `bump --help` is the whole story.

INSTALLING AN APPLICATION DOES NOT RUN IT (ADR-015 §3.2.2). `enabled`
is the operator's and lives in the machine's document, so an install on
its own leaves the application idle with nothing to diagnose. `install
--enable` writes it for you; `install --help` is the whole story.

THE MANIFEST IS `[package.metadata.rivet]` IN YOUR Cargo.toml. It is a
REQUEST, not a description -- ADR-015 §3.3. These are the keys and the
only values each accepts:

  kind             = daemon | oneshot | socket-activated
  restart          = always | on-failure | never
  ready            = none | notify | listening
  network          = none | egress | group:<name>
  state            = none | private
  memory           = 128M          -- digits, then K, M or G
  cpu              = 0.5           -- decimal cores; ADR-015 §3
  devices          = ["display", "input"]
  library          = ["<name>-<version>-<64 hex>"]   -- see `library`
  listen           = ["tcp:8080", "tcp:8443:direct", "udp:53", "unix:name"]
  connects         = ["<owner>:<endpoint>"]
  provides         = ["socket:<endpoint>"]
  title            = "Aura Controller"  -- what a PERSON calls it
  settings         = ["<name>"]     -- ADR-038; declared, not valued
  proxy-path       = <one segment>  -- https://<host>/<segment>/
  proxy-auth       = operator | none    -- absent means operator
  proxy-auth-paths = ["none:pair", "operator:pair/admin"]
  backup-path      = api/v1/backup  -- relative to proxy-path
  backup-format    = sqlite | csv | json | tar
  backup-feed      = api/v1/blobs   -- the OTHER shape; not both
  accepts-class    = ["temperature-sensor"]  -- ADR-053; absent/empty takes no addon
  restore-path     = api/v1/restore -- needs backup-path; operator-gated
  material         = ["fleet-tls"]  -- ADR-055; per-machine, operator-installed

THIS LIST IS THE WHOLE OF IT. It was six keys short from 2026-09-02
until 2026-09-08 -- memory, title, settings and all three proxy keys
existed, were accepted, and were documented nowhere a person types.

`backup-path` + `backup-format` say WHERE this application serves a
backup and WHAT one fetch returns; `backup-feed` is the other shape, a
resumable collection, and a manifest may not declare both. Either needs
a `proxy-path` to be relative to. `cargo rivet backup` is what reads
them -- ADR-051. `restore-path` says where the application accepts that
backup BACK; it needs `backup-path` and `backup-format`, the route must
require an operator certificate, and `cargo rivet restore` sends to it.

`material` NAMES A KIND, NEVER A FILE -- ADR-055 §3. `fleet-tls` is
tls-cert, tls-key and tls-root, the three files an application serving
HTTPS behind rivet-proxyd reads out of its own data directory, and the
same three a caller presenting a client certificate reads. They are
PER-MACHINE and per-operator: `install` never mints them (R-194), it
refuses to put an application into service without them and prints the
`rivet-provision ca server` and `cargo rivet secrets` lines that install
them. Declare it and the refusal arrives before the payload does;
declare nothing and install says nothing, exactly as it always has.

A PROXIED APPLICATION'S PORTS LISTEN ON 127.0.0.1 (ADR-046 §7). With a
`proxy-path`, every `tcp:` and `udp:` port binds loopback, so only
rivet-proxyd and the machine's own programs reach it. A port that must be
reached directly -- a phone's listener -- says `tcp:8443:direct`. The
routed port (the first tcp one) may not be `:direct`, and `:direct` needs
a `proxy-path`: without one every port already binds every address.

THERE IS NO `kind = "kiosk"`. An application is a kiosk one because it
declares devices = ["display"], and it is then OFFERED on the launcher's
menu rather than started (ADR-036 §8A). `examples/templates/` has a
working manifest of each shape, with the reasoning beside every key.

`run` performs ONE operation from the machine's own catalogue over
ADR-035's control plane and prints the machine's answer, unchanged —
`-- get storage`, `-- apply reload confirm`. It is how you ask a board a
question without opening a shell on it.

`screenshot` fetches a capture from a board and writes it as a PNG. A
Rivet photographs its screen as QOI, because an encoder is sixty lines
on a device where a compressor is a dependency; turning one back into a
picture is this end's job. IT DOES NOT TAKE THE PICTURE — the launcher
does that when it is sent `apply input capture`, and it refuses while an
application holds the display. `screenshot --help` says why that matters.

`fleet` is ADR-052's FLEET REPOSITORY — a git-tracked manifest and a
digest-keyed object store, on THIS workstation, naming every signed
artifact the fleet is built from. `fleet init` makes one, `fleet
publish FILE.rvt --trusted-key PATH` verifies and stores an artifact,
`fleet list` reads it back. `install` publishes into it before it
sends, and `install --artifact ID` sends one it holds. NOT `rivet-fleet` (a different binary) and NOT `[repos.<name>]`
(a git repository a Rivet MACHINE hosts, managed by `rivet-fleet add
repo`) — `fleet --help` says so again, at length.

`cargo rivet update --help`, `install --help`, `run --help`,
`screenshot --help` and `fleet --help` for those verbs' options.

package options:
  --manifest-path PATH  the crate's Cargo.toml (default ./Cargo.toml)
  --signing-key PATH    32 raw bytes, or 64 hex characters. Optional
                        since 2026-08-30: without it, $RIVET_APP_SEED
                        then ~/.rivet/keys/rivet-app.seed. If neither
                        is there the refusal names all three and says
                        what a board will accept. NOT the same key as
                        `cargo rivet identity new`, which mints a TLS
                        identity
  --target TRIPLE       default aarch64-unknown-linux-musl
  --profile NAME        cargo profile (default release)
  --bin NAME            which binary (default: the package name)
  --binary PATH         use this already-built binary and run no
                        cargo build at all
  --target-dir DIR      cargo's target directory (default <crate>/target)
  --out-dir DIR         where the .rvt goes (default <crate>/target/rivet)
  --asset NAME=PATH     an extra member, repeatable (ADR-015 §3)
  --no-assets           do not walk <crate>/assets/
  --public-key-out PATH write the PUBLIC key here, 32 raw bytes
  --print-manifest      render [package.metadata.rivet] and print it.
                        Builds nothing, signs nothing, needs no key —
                        only --manifest-path is read alongside it.
                        For a harness that needs a rendered manifest
                        and would otherwise hand-copy one
                        (SDK-Adoption-Friction.md §2.3)

EVERY FILE IN <crate>/assets/ IS PACKAGED, with no flag and no list.
`aura-renderer` shipped without its four typefaces because --asset is
easy not to type, exited on a missing face, and left a board's screen
black for hours with the display hand-over working perfectly
(PLAN.md §119.3). Members are FLAT — 32 bytes, no path separator, each
installed beside the program — so a subdirectory under assets/ is
refused rather than flattened into a path your program will not open.
--no-assets turns the walk off; --asset still adds to it.

The output name is composed from what the tool knows and there is no
override — ADR-027 §7. An application carries no <platform> component.

$RIVET_PACKAGE_DIRTY overrides whether the version is `-dirty`, when
set to one of 1/true/yes/dirty or 0/false/no/clean. Unset (the
default), the tree's dirty state is asked of the git this runs with —
which is wrong inside this project's build container on an otherwise
clean tree (AGENTS.md §10.5). The escape is one fact, not a whole
describe string: git rev-parse and git describe --exact-match do not
disagree between the two gits, only git status --porcelain does.

key options:
  new --out PATH        ask the OPERATING SYSTEM for 32 bytes and write
                        them there. It REFUSES an existing file: every
                        board that trusts the public half would refuse
                        every future update, and there is no backup
  --out PATH            write the PUBLIC key here, 64 hex characters
  backup DIR            encrypt ~/.rivet/keys' seed(s) under a passphrase
                        (asked twice, no echo) and write them to DIR.
                        `key backup --help` for the file format and why
                        a forgotten passphrase cannot be recovered from.
  restore DIR           decrypt DIR's seed(s) back to ~/.rivet/keys.
                        Refuses a wrong passphrase or an existing seed —
                        `--replace` overrides only the second.
The seed is read and never printed, on any path.

START WITH `cargo rivet setup`. It mints both signing seeds, your
control-plane identity and the board's, in the order they depend on
each other, and skips whatever is already there. Running the four
commands by hand works and gets the ORDER wrong, which is how a card
comes to be built before the key it is supposed to be built against.

`setup --check` reports what this host holds and mints nothing.
Never commit a seed (AGENTS.md §8.3).
```

### `rivet-fleet`

```
The fleet register: enroll machines, compose their documents, reach them.

Usage: rivet-fleet [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  update   Update to the latest version
  get      Read one thing out of the register.
  set      Change one value on a record.
  list     Everything of a kind.
  add      Put something into the register.
  remove   Take something out of the register.
  apply    Do something to a machine.
  export   Produce a document.
  explain  Where a value came from.
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --update               Update to the latest version
      --identity <identity>  This OPERATOR's own control-plane identity — a directory `cargo rivet identity new` wrote. Without it this tool can reach no machine over ADR-035's control plane.
      --pin <pin>            The machine's public key, 64 hex characters. A device record that carries one is used without this; `set pin` records one and `add identity` records the key it mints. This OVERRIDES the record, for a machine whose key has been replaced and whose record is not caught up yet. A device with neither is a refusal, not a connection without pinning.
  -h, --help                 Print help
  -V, --version              Print version
```

### `rivet-provision`

```
Compose and validate a Rivet provisioning document.

Usage: rivet-provision

Options:
  -h, --help     Print help
  -V, --version  Print version

Verbs (matched before the parser, so they do not appear above):

  rivet-provision ca <suffixes> <fleet-name> <directory> [operator-name] [--no-install]
          Mint the fleet's certificate authority, its root, and your own browser
          identity. Files the identity into your Windows Personal store.

          --no-install  Write browser.pfx and DO NOT touch the certificate
                        store. This is how the ceremony is rehearsed: certutil
                        lives in the system directory, so there is no other way
                        to run `ca` without adding a certificate to the store
                        you are rehearsing for.

  rivet-provision ca server <hostname> <directory> [--names <list>]
          Mint a fleet server's certificate. By DEFAULT it composes
          <hostname>.<suffix> for every suffix the authority permits, read out
          of root.crt. --names takes a literal comma-separated list instead,
          for somebody who means exactly those names and no others.

  rivet-provision ca backup <directory> [--replace]
          Copy the authority (~/.rivet/ca) to <directory>. REQUIRED: there is
          no default location for storing secret keys. Reports every file
          copied, with its size. Refuses to overwrite a backup already at
          <directory> unless --replace is given.

  rivet-provision ca restore <directory> [--replace] [--no-install]
          Copy the authority back from a backup at <directory>, and
          re-install root.crt into the Windows Root store and browser.pfx
          into Personal — the inverse of `rivet-reset`, not of a plain copy.
          Refuses to restore over an authority already at ~/.rivet/ca unless
          --replace is given. --no-install writes the files and does not
          touch the certificate store; use it for every rehearsal.

  rivet-provision stage --document <path> --identity <dir> [--at <dir>]
                        [--fleet-root <fleet> [--suffixes <list>]] [--passkeys <file>]
          Build the ADR-049 staging bundle for a server or member document
          that has none, without the interview: the role, hostname and
          addressing come from the document, the authority from <at>/ca. It
          is written beside the document and listed by name and size, never
          by content. cargo rivet provision and write-image run it themselves
          when a server or member document has no bundle. --fleet-root makes
          a server's card carry a request instead: the machine mints the
          fleet's root and its own certificate on first boot (ADR-063).
          --passkeys carries a proxy's passkeys file to the new card.

Run with no arguments for the menu. On a workstation with no authority it
first asks whether you are starting a new fleet or joining an existing one,
and mints nothing until you answer (ADR-063 section 8). A new fleet's root
is minted here (1), or on its fleet server's first boot (3, fleet-root mode).

  rivet-provision --new-fleet
          Answer that question in advance: this is a new fleet, so mint its
          authority. Without a terminal to ask at, the menu refuses rather than
          mint unless this is given.
```

### `rivet-reset`

```
rivet-reset — return this workstation to the state a first-ever run would find.

SPEC-05 §2, and step 1 of the twelve. It removes the fleet's certificate
authority, the register, the provisioning documents composed here, and the
authority's certificates from the Windows stores — the root AND every leaf it
issued. --keep-authority is the other mode: it empties the fleet and keeps all
of the authority.

usage: rivet-reset [options]

  --ca DIR           the authority. Default ~/.rivet/ca
  --register DIR     the fleet register. Default: where rivet-fleet keeps it,
                     resolved through the same loader that tool uses, so a
                     configuration file and RIVET_FLEET_REGISTER both count
  --provision DIR    composed documents and answer notebooks. Default
                     ~/.rivet/provision
  --root FILE        the authority's root certificate, if it is not in --ca.
                     This is what the certificate store is matched against
  --verdict FILE     ask what this program would decide about ONE certificate
                     file — PEM or DER — against --root, and stop. No store is
                     opened and nothing is removed. May be given more than once
  --include-retired  also remove authorities in the store that carry this
                     authority's SUBJECT NAME and a different key, and the
                     leaves they issued. These are listed either way; without
                     the flag they are left alone
  --backup DIR       where to look for a backup of the authority — made with
                     `rivet-provision ca backup DIR`. root.crt is compared
                     byte for byte against DIR and one level of its
                     subdirectories; the report says what was found
  --proceed-without-backup
                     required to remove the authority when no backup was
                     found. Without --backup at all counts as none found.
                     Not required under --dry-run, which removes nothing
  --dry-run          print the report and stop. Removes nothing, asks nothing
  --confirm          proceed without the interactive question. The report is
                     printed first either way
  --keep-authority   start the FLEET again and KEEP the authority. See below
  --fleet DIR        the fleet repository. Default ~/.rivet/fleet.
                     --keep-authority only
  --armada DIR       the Armada Registry. Default ~/.rivet/armada.
                     --keep-authority only
  -h, --help         this text

--keep-authority — a new fleet under the same authority (SPEC-05 §2)

  The authority's root and your browser certificate stay installed, so nothing
  about the browser is redone. Every record of the old fleet's machines goes:

    the register          every device record, the fleet file, and the
                          credential store beside them (--register)
    the fleet repository  register/ and documents/, removed with git and
                          committed as one commit naming this program. A
                          repository with uncommitted changes is REFUSED
                          before anything anywhere is removed (--fleet)
    provisioning          composed documents, staging bundles and answer
                          notebooks (--provision)
    the Armada            every Fleet it lists, fleets/*.toml (--armada)

  KEPT, and named in the report: the authority directory (--ca), the Windows
  certificate stores (never opened in this mode), the fleet repository's
  manifest.toml and objects/ (the published software), the Armada's own
  armada.toml (where backups go), the signing seeds and the identities.
  --backup is not needed, because the authority is not removed.
  --include-retired, --root and --verdict are refused with it.

    rivet-reset --keep-authority --dry-run     the plan; removes nothing
    rivet-reset --keep-authority --confirm     do it without asking

WHAT IT WILL NOT REMOVE, and there is no flag for any of it:

  ~/.rivet/keys/*.seed       the signing seeds. Every board's trust store holds
                             their public halves; removing them invalidates
                             every payload this project has ever signed
  ~/.rivet/identity          the control-plane operator identity, which reaches
                             every running board
  anything under .ssh        no tool of this maintainer's touches an SSH key

CERTIFICATES ARE MATCHED ON THE AUTHORITY'S KEY, NOT ITS NAME. A re-minted
authority may carry the same subject as the one it replaced — on 2026-09-07 one
did — so a matcher that compared names would delete an authority you meant to
keep. Every certificate here is one whose signature this authority's public key
verifies.
```

---

## Board-side binaries

Ship on the card. `--help` is checked here, inside the build container, against the same source `cargo build --workspace --bins` compiles for every other check in this repository — it is not run against a board and does not stand in for one (`AGENTS.md` §10.5's own rule: *"it works in QEMU" is not "it works", and neither is "it compiles"*).

### `rivet`

```
rivet — Rivet's administration CLI, and the binary /etc/shells names.

    rivet [--output json|text] <verb> [...]
    rivet get schema
    rivet measure hash <path>
    rivet --version
    rivet --help

Verbs (ADR-006 §6.4's closed set): get, set, list, add, remove, apply, plan,
export, explain. THIS BUILD IMPLEMENTS THREE OF THEM.
`get` reads TWENTY subjects; `apply` takes TWENTY-NINE subjects.
`apply restart` restarts the MACHINE; `apply service-restart <name>` restarts ONE SERVICE.
START WITH `rivet get catalogue` IF YOU DO NOT KNOW WHAT THIS MACHINE CAN DO: it is
the catalogue above, over the wire, and it is the one command that needs no shell.

THE LIST BELOW IS NOT ALL OF THEM AND IS NOT THE AUTHORITY. It shows the few
that need prose to use safely. `rivet --version` publishes the operation
catalogue, generated from the types; that is the authority for what exists, and
`rivet get schema` is the authority for the document. Ask one of those rather
than this text.

    rivet get log [boot] [limit] [--follow [--for <seconds>|forever]]
                             this machine's journal (ADR-022 §9) — what it did,
                             in the order it did it. `boot` is `latest` (the
                             default), `previous` (the one before this — what to
                             ask after a board came back), `all`, or a boot
                             identifier. It cannot be selected by TIME: a Pi has
                             no RTC, so every boot starts at the epoch until
                             something corrects it (ADR-021). Records come back
                             as the lines the machine wrote; in nushell:
                               rivet get log | from json | get records
                                 | each { from json } | where sev == error
                             `limit` DEFAULTS TO 200 — the last 200 records, not
                             all of them (ADR-022 §9.6). The word `all` is how to
                             ask for everything the journal still holds.
                             `--follow` streams instead of answering: one record
                             per line as it is written, stdout carrying nothing
                             else, until `--for` runs out (300 seconds by
                             default, or `forever`). In nushell:
                               rivet get log latest 20 --follow --for 60
                                 | each { from json }
    rivet get storage      how full every mounted filesystem is (ADR-005
                             §4.1.3) — what it is, where it is mounted, its type,
                             total/used/available bytes, and which of Rivet's
                             own locations it holds. NOTHING IS FILTERED; select
                             in the shell:
                               rivet get storage | from json | get filesystems
                                 | where mount-point == /state
                             /system is a DIRECTORY in the root filesystem and
                             not a mount point, so look for it in `holds` rather
                             than as a row of its own. capacity-percent and the
                             inode fields are ABSENT on a filesystem that has no
                             such number — /proc is one on every machine — so
                             `select` them with a trailing ?:
                               ... | select mount-point capacity-percent? holds?
    rivet explain <path>   what generates a path, and what to change instead
    rivet apply trial-boot <a|b> [confirm]
                             arm a one-shot trial boot of the other A/B slot
    rivet apply power-off [confirm]
                             stop the machine and leave it off
    rivet apply restart [confirm]
                             stop the machine and bring it back on the DEFAULT
                             slot. An armed trial boot is NOT taken by this
    rivet apply trial-restart [confirm]
                             stop the machine and bring it back ONCE in the slot
                             a trial boot armed (ADR-018 §5.1). This is the only
                             restart that carries the firmware's one-shot flag
    rivet apply service-restart <name> [confirm]
                             restart ONE SERVICE and nothing else — NOT the
                             machine. This is how a deployed application starts
                             running the bytes you shipped (ADR-017 §6).
                             It may only ask the supervisor to CONVERGE toward
                             the desired-state document: it restarts a service
                             the document enables, and starts an enabled one
                             that is idle, failed, backing off or done. It
                             REFUSES to start a service the document disables.
                             To change what this machine should be running,
                             edit the document:
                               rivet apply edit /state/config/machine.toml ...
                               rivet apply reload confirm
                             The plan comes from the supervisor itself, so it
                             names the state your service is actually in. If the
                             service you name is the one carrying this request —
                             rivet-mcpd — the answer may not arrive; a dropped
                             connection is normal there and `rivet get status`
                             is what says whether it worked.
    rivet apply service-stop <name> [confirm]
                             stop ONE APPLICATION and keep it stopped — it is
                             not restarted as a crash — without uninstalling it.
                             Its files and data under /state/app are untouched
                             and `enabled` in the document is not changed. The
                             stop lasts until `service-start`, or until the next
                             boot, which returns the machine to its document.
                             REFUSED for rivet-mcpd and rivet-netd, which carry
                             the way in, and for every other image service.
    rivet apply service-start <name> [confirm]
                             release a `service-stop`; the application then runs
                             again if the document enables it. Refused for a
                             service that was not stopped that way.
    rivet apply clock-floor-reset [confirm]
                             make the running clock this machine's clock floor
                             (ADR-021 §3): the time the next boot restores the
                             clock to at the least. The floor only rises on its
                             own, so a clock once stepped to a wrong future is
                             restored to it at every boot until this lowers it.
                             The plan names the floor now and the running clock
                             that would replace it. Correct the running clock
                             first if it is wrong: the floor follows it.
    rivet apply uninstall-library <product|reference> [confirm]
                             remove an installed LIBRARY. A product name removes
                             every build of that product under /state/lib; a
                             full reference <name>-<version>-<64 hex> removes
                             exactly one. REFUSED, removing nothing, if an
                             installed application names a build it would
                             remove in its manifest's `library` closure, or if
                             an application's manifest cannot be read. An
                             application that only accepts the library's class
                             is named in the plan and loses the addon at its
                             next start: nothing running is restarted, and the
                             supervisor recomposes every service's library path
                             without a reboot.

Every other verb refuses with E_UNIMPLEMENTED. `rivet --version` publishes the
operation catalogue, generated from the types, which is the authority for what
exists; `rivet schema` publishes the configuration document's JSON Schema.

schema and measure are NOT verbs and are not in ADR-006 §6.4's closed set; they
are not in the operation catalogue either, and Verb::parse refuses both.

    rivet measure hash <path>
                             hash a block device or file with BLAKE3 and SHA-256
                             in one streaming pass, reporting bytes, elapsed
                             milliseconds, MB/s and both digests. It changes
                             nothing. This exists to settle ADR-029 §7.2 and
                             ADR-015 §4.2 on real hardware:
                               rivet measure hash /dev/mmcblk0p3
                             The per-algorithm times exclude the card — read time
                             is reported separately — and MB means 10^6 bytes.

apply changes the machine, so it confirms first (ADR-012 §7.1): without the
final word `confirm` it reads the machine, checks the safety interlocks, changes
nothing, and refuses with the plan. A misspelt `confirm` is refused rather than
read as absence.

trial-boot NEVER reboots — arming and restarting are two acts (ADR-018 §5), and
it says which restart the arming needs. The three stop subjects never arm.
So a trial boot on this hardware is two commands, in this order:

    rivet apply trial-boot b confirm      arm it
    rivet apply trial-restart confirm     take it

The stop subjects ask pid 1, which owns shutdown (ADR-017 §3.1.5 item 6): it
stops the supervisor, waits for it, syncs the filesystems, and only then asks
the kernel. So the machine has NOT stopped when this command answers, and the
answer races the shutdown of whatever channel carried the request — ADR-035's
control plane, or a session on the machine — so the client may print the answer
and exit 0, or may report a dropped connection, and both are normal. Read the
console for what happened after it.

rivet REFUSES to signal pid 1 unless /proc/1/comm is exactly `rivet-initd`,
and refuses if it cannot read it. On a development host pid 1 is that host's own
init, and this command would otherwise stop the machine you are working on.

Output is structured first (ADR-006 §4). A terminal gets the human rendering
and a pipe gets JSON; --output forces either.

From a workstation (ADR-035 — the control plane is the only transport):
  cargo rivet run --host <host>:7777 --identity <dir> --pin <hex> -- <command>
  cargo rivet run --show -- <command>   prints the tool call, sends nothing

The login-shell behaviour below is DORMANT. Nothing in this image execs rivet
as a shell; it is still described because a card built before ADR-035
behaves this way:
  a bare login          refused, E_NO_INTERACTIVE_SHELL — nushell is the ruled
                        interactive shell and is not in this image
  "rivet ..."           runs that command
  "anything-else"       refused, E_NOT_A_SHELL — rivet executes no programs,
                        which is also why a remote file copy never worked
                        against a Rivet host (PLAN.md §4.26)

Exit codes: 0 a value; 1 the operation refused; 2 the arguments were not
usable; 126 an interactive session was asked for; 127 -c named a program.
```

### `rivet-bluetoothd`

```
usage: rivet-bluetoothd

Reads BLE advertisements and hands them to the one application that declares
connects = ["rivet-bluetoothd:advertisements"]. Takes no arguments: the adapter is asked of the
kernel and the socket is handed over by the supervisor (ADR-041).
```

### `rivet-deploy`

```
rivet-deploy — install a signed .rvt into this machine's inactive slot. ADR-029 §9.2.

usage: rivet-deploy [options] <payload.rvt>

  --trusted-key PATH   a 32-byte Ed25519 public key, raw or hex, to accept
                       INSTEAD of this machine's own trust store. Repeatable,
                       and NOT required: by default the store the image
                       carries at /system/trust answers, which is what
                       ADR-028 5.5.6 means by a machine saying what it trusts.
                       An override is for a card built --no-trust, or for a
                       key that is not on this machine. It is journalled at
                       warn, and it is narrowed to `update` alone.
  --dry-run            verify the payload and plan the install, writing
                       nothing. Reaches the same verdict the real run would,
                       so a refusal is discovered before a confirmation
                       rather than after it (ADR-006 §6.2).
  --no-read-back       do not re-read the written system partition and hash
                       it. ADR-029 §9.2 step 9 recommends the read-back and
                       says why: SD cards do accept writes and store something
                       else, and this is the only defence against that. It
                       costs one 640 MiB read.
  --text               render records as text rather than as ADR-022 §3's
                       JSONL. The JSONL form is what the supervisor's capture
                       parses back into records (ADR-022 §4), so it is the
                       default and --text is for a human at a terminal.
  --help

It installs and arms; it does NOT reboot. ADR-029 §9.1 — an armed machine is
inert until a trial reboot, so twenty machines can be installed at noon and
rebooted at 2am.
```

### `rivet-fleetd` — exits 1 against `--help`

```
rivet-fleetd: "--help" is not something this program takes. It is a daemon the supervisor starts with no arguments; the one other form is `rivet-fleetd converge [--dry-run]`, which makes one fleet-as-code pass and exits.
```

### `rivet-image` — exits 1 against `--help`

```
rivet-image: usage: rivet-image OUT.img INIT SUPERVISOR CLI NETD TIMED MDNSD
                     GIT HTTP-BACKEND DEPLOY MCPD
                     [--nushell PATH] [--femto PATH] [--splash PATH]
                     [--bluetoothd PATH]
                     [--ca-bundle PATH] [--zoneinfo DIR]
                     [--gdbserver PATH] [--strace PATH] [--device-mib N] [--default-slot a|b]
                     [--document PATH] [--fleet-repository DIR] [--identity DIR]
                     [--staging PATH] [--launcher PATH] [--displayd PATH]
                     [--proxyd PATH] [--dnsd PATH] [--application PATH]...

  OUT.img      the image file to write
  INIT         the rivet-initd binary, static aarch64
  SUPERVISOR   the rivet-sysd binary, static aarch64
  CLI          the rivet binary, static aarch64 — also a login shell
  NETD         the rivet-netd binary, static aarch64
  TIMED        the rivet-timed binary, static aarch64 — ADR-021 §7's
               SNTP client. The supervisor's service definition has
               named this path since before a card carried it
  MDNSD        the rivet-mdnsd binary, static aarch64 — PLAN.md §23s
               responder. The supervisor names this path and ships the
               service DISABLED, so the card carries it and does not
               run it until the document says so
  GIT          the git binary, static aarch64 — NOT built by this
               workspace. tools/buildroot/build.sh leaves it at
               <output>/target/usr/bin/git (ADR-009 §6). ONE file:
               the git-core directory beside it is 147 hardlinks to
               this same inode and every verb Rivet needs is a
               builtin reached as `git <verb>` (PLAN.md §43.6)
  HTTP-BACKEND git-http-backend, static aarch64 - ADR-035 4s smart HTTP.
               NOT built by this workspace and NOT the same file as GIT:
               buildroot leaves it at target/usr/libexec/git-core/, and
               PLAN.md 84.1 measured the inodes to prove it is its own
               binary rather than a builtin. It needs /system/bin on PATH
               at RUNTIME or it serves empty repositories (PLAN.md 85.2).
  DEPLOY       the rivet-deploy binary, static aarch64 — ADR-029 §14's
               installer. NOTHING ON THE CARD STARTS IT: how a payload
               reaches it is not ruled (the maintainer's 2026-08-24 install-request ruling). Required anyway,
               because a card that cannot install an update is not a
               variant, it is a card that can never be updated
  MCPD         the rivet-mcpd binary, static aarch64 — ADR-035s control
               plane, and since phase 3 the WHOLE administration
               surface. The supervisor names this path and ships the
               service ENABLED (ADR-023 4.1), so a card built without
               it boots to a board nothing can reach

  --identity DIR the device's TLS identity, as `cargo rivet identity new`
                 writes it: device.seed, device.crt and a peers file
                 beside them. ALL THREE OR NONE. They go on the BOOT
                 partition; PID 1 copies them to /state/secrets on first
                 boot and DELETES the seed from the card (ADR-019 3.1).
                 A card without one boots, and its control plane refuses
                 to start -- visible in `rivet get status`, costing no
                 other service.
  --staging PATH the staging bundle rivet-provision writes: the
                 certificates, keys and fleet register an APPLICATION
                 on this machine is handed before it first starts.
                 Same journey as --identity -- it goes on the BOOT
                 partition, PID 1 copies it to /state/staging and
                 DELETES it from the card, and the SUPERVISOR then
                 delivers each application's share into the data
                 directory it owns, with that application's uid. The
                 extra hop is the point: the uid is derived at
                 discovery and is not knowable here (ADR-049).
                 The file is PARSED before the card is written, so a
                 bundle that will not read is refused on your
                 workstation rather than on a headless board.
  --application PATH
                 a signed .rvt this card CARRIES -- ADR-050 4.
                 REPEATABLE; each names one payload. It rides on the
                 BOOT partition beside the document, the identity and
                 the staging bundle; PID 1 lands it in /state/carried
                 on the first boot and the supervisor asks
                 rivet-deploy to install it, which is the same route
                 `cargo rivet deploy` takes afterwards.
                 VERIFIED HERE, against the trust store THIS image is
                 about to carry -- so a payload signed by a key this
                 card would refuse is refused on your workstation
                 rather than on a headless board. The name on the card
                 comes from the payload's SIGNED header, not from the
                 file you named.
                 NOT SECRET and NOT deleted from the card: a .rvt is
                 protected by its signature, so the card keeps saying
                 what it was built to carry.
  --launcher PATH
                 the rivet-launcher binary, static aarch64 -- ADR-050
                 2.1's tier 2. OPTIONAL, and the service ships
                 DISABLED like rivet-bluetoothd's, so a card carrying
                 it shows no menu until the document says so. A card
                 without it is a supported headless machine.
  --displayd PATH
                 the rivet-displayd binary -- ADR-058 4.1's
                 compositor, on the launcher's tier and its terms.
                 OPTIONAL. It is DYNAMIC, and the only binary of
                 Rivet's own that is, so a card carrying it must
                 also carry libgbm, libxkbcommon and libgcc_s.
  --proxyd PATH
                 the rivet-proxyd binary, static aarch64 -- ADR-060's
                 front door, part of the operating system and run under
                 its own uid and Landlock ruleset. OPTIONAL here, and
                 the service ships DISABLED: the document's role turns
                 it on. tools/card/build.sh always passes it.
  --dnsd PATH
                 the rivet-dnsd binary, static aarch64 -- ADR-047's name
                 service. OPTIONAL, and the service ships DISABLED: a
                 document with `[services.rivet-dnsd] enabled = true`
                 and a `[dns]` table turns it on.
  --kernel PATH       the kernel for the boot partition, as an
                        uncompressed arm64 Image. Buildroot leaves it
                        at <output>/images/Image. WITHOUT THIS the build

                        fetch-kernel.sh copied off a Raspberry Pi OS
                        board - somebody else's kernel, whose modular
                        wireless stack cannot load on a Rivet image
                        (PLAN.md §102.25). Goes with --device-tree.
  --device-tree PATH    the device tree for that kernel, Buildroot's
                        <output>/images/bcm2711-rpi-4-b.dtb. Required
                        with --kernel and refused without it.
  --supplicant PATH     wpa_supplicant, static aarch64 - ADR-004 §3's
                        PERMANENT Tier C dependency. Buildroot leaves it
                        at <output>/target/usr/sbin/wpa_supplicant.
                        Omit it for a card with no wireless, which is
                        a supported machine.
  --wpa-cli PATH        wpa_cli. A BRING-UP tool: it proves the C side
                        associates independently of rivet-netd, so a
                        failure has one candidate cause not two.
  --udhcpc PATH         the DHCP client. Buildroot leaves it at
                        <output>/target/bin/busybox, built with exactly
                        ONE applet; it is installed as `udhcpc` because
                        that is what it is.
  --wifi-firmware DIR   the CYW43455 firmware directory, Buildroot's
                        <output>/target/lib/firmware/brcm. FOUR files
                        are taken: three for the WIRELESS half by the
                        names ADR-004 §8.1 measured, and one for the
                        BLUETOOTH half added by R-144 — the flag is
                        still called --wifi-firmware because it names
                        one directory, and both halves live in it.
                        A missing clm_blob does not fail, it makes
                        association MISBEHAVE; a missing .hcd means no
                        Bluetooth controller ever appears.
  --splash PATH  the rivet-splash binary, static aarch64. PID 1 runs it
                 on an ordinary boot and NOT on a trial boot, so a
                 trial shows the console it is being watched for
  --bluetoothd PATH
                 the rivet-bluetoothd binary, static aarch64 — ADR-041's
                 BLE observer. OPTIONAL, and paired with the KERNEL
                 rather than with a screen: it needs CONFIG_BT, which no
                 kernel built before 2026-09-05 has. The service ships
                 DISABLED, so a card carrying it does not hold the radio
  --femto PATH   the femto binary, static aarch64 — ADR-005 §5.5.1's
               editor. A card without one is a supported card.
  --nushell PATH the nu binary, static aarch64 — ADR-005 §5.1's login
               shell. OPTIONAL: without it the
               card's login shell is the CLI, which is every card built
               before 2026-08-24. tools/nushell/build.sh produces it
  --gdbserver PATH the gdbserver stub, static aarch64 — ADR-005 §7.
               OPTIONAL, and whether a card SHOULD carry one is
               ADR-005 §7.4 and unruled. tools/debug/build.sh
               produces it; nothing on the card starts it
  --strace PATH  strace, static aarch64 — ADR-005 §7.2. OPTIONAL, on
               the same terms
  --arch TOKEN   REQUIRED. ADR-027 §3's token for the target the
               binaries were built for: aarch64, armv6 or x86_64.
               Recorded at /system/arch; the machine refuses every
               artifact built for anything else
  --device-mib   size of the card, in MiB (default 2048)
  --default-slot which slot a fresh card boots (default a)
  --document PATH the first-boot provisioning document, written as
                rivet.toml onto BOTH boot partitions. Without one
                the card carries a template declaring a schema
                version and nothing else -- which boots to a machine
                nobody can reach, because it takes no address.
                NOT validated here unless --fleet-repository is
                also given: without it, this crate does not depend
                on rivet-config's parser, so a bad document is
                refused by the BOARD on first boot.
  --fleet-repository DIR
                resolve --document's enabled application services

                5.1. Requires --document. Additive with

Produces an image file. It does NOT write a card — do that yourself,
with a device path you typed, once you have checked it.
```

### `rivet-mcpd` — exits 2 against `--help`

```
rivet-mcpd: rivet-mcpd — the MCP control plane (ADR-035 phase 1)

  --document PATH  the configuration document. Its [control-plane]
                   table says where to bind; without the table, or
                   without this flag, the address is 127.0.0.1:7777.
  --listen ADDR    bind THIS instead, whatever the document says.
                   For running one by hand; the supervisor never
                   passes it.
  --identity DIR   this machine's TLS identity: device.seed and
                   device.crt, as `cargo rivet identity new` writes them.
  --peers FILE     the Ed25519 public keys allowed to connect, one
                   hex key per line. `#` starts a comment.

It hands each connection the stdin and stdout of `/system/bin/rivet mcp`.
It speaks no JSON-RPC of its own and never will (ADR-011).

WITH --identity AND --peers every connection is mutually authenticated
(ADR-035 §7.2 over ADR-025 §2) and ANY address may be bound.

WITHOUT THEM there is no encryption and no identity, so this binds
LOOPBACK ONLY and refuses any other address by name. A control plane
reachable from a network with no authentication is not a smaller
version of the design.

ONE WITHOUT THE OTHER IS REFUSED: half a trust model is not one.
```

```
rivet-mdnsd: `--help` is not an option this program takes. usage: rivet-mdnsd --projection <path>
```

### `rivet-netd`

```
rivet-netd — converge this machine's interfaces onto the configuration
document, which is the only thing that says what they should be (ADR-007 §3.3).

    rivet-netd --document <path>
    rivet-netd --help

The document's [network] table names one entry per interface, each declaring
`method = "static"` with an `address` (and an optional `gateway`), or
`method = "dhcp"`.

It converges once and exits. A dhcp interface's address comes from the lease
its supervised client recorded under /run/rivet/dhcp; with no lease yet it is
left for the supervisor to run this again when one arrives (ADR-004 §8).
```

### `rivet-smbd` — exits 2 against `--help`

```
rivet-smbd: rivet-smbd — SMB file sharing (PLAN.md §23.5, §57, §69)

  --listen ADDR        REQUIRED. Where to bind, e.g. 0.0.0.0:445.
  --share NAME=PATH    REQUIRED, repeatable. A share and the directory it serves.
  --user NAME          The one account that may connect. Its password comes from
                       RIVET_SMBD_PASSWORD, never from an argument: /proc/<pid>/cmdline
                       is world-readable. Without this, shares are PUBLIC.
  --read-only          Serve every share read-only.

There is no default listen address, no default share and no configuration file.
ADR-007 has no [shares] table yet, and PLAN.md §23.5 item 1 makes adding one a
ruling rather than a detail — the absence of encryption has to be a decision an
operator states, not one they discover.
```

### `rivet-timed`

```
rivet-timed — Rivet's time client (ADR-021 §4, §7)

  --server <ip[:port]>   a time server, by ADDRESS. Repeatable; tried in order.
                         Port defaults to 123. A hostname is refused: a
                         Rivet image ships no /etc/resolv.conf (ADR-008 §5.1.1).
                         The clock is stepped only when two different servers
                         agree, so one server alone never moves it (ADR-021 §3).
  --poll-seconds <n>     seconds between polls. Default 1024.
  --once                 poll once, act on it, and exit.
  --text | --jsonl       console form. Default jsonl (ADR-022 §3).
  --help                 this.

Exit codes with --once: 0 a server answered, 1 none did, 2 argv was not usable.
```

### `femto`

```
femto 0.1.137 — a tiny editor for Rivet.

usage: femto <file>

Arrow keys move, typing inserts, and the two lines at the bottom of the
screen are the keys. ^O writes, ^X exits, ^G explains.

Files under /etc are a read-only view of state owned elsewhere
(ADR-007 §3.6.2). femto opens them, refuses to write them, and says what
to change instead. `rivet explain <path>` is the same answer as a
structured value.
```

---

## Not generated

| Binary | Why |
| :-- | :-- |
| `rivet-launcher` | cross-only: cmd/rivet-launcher links libdrm from the aarch64 sysroot (AGENTS.md §10, the template-kiosk three flags). The container's own architecture has no libdrm to link against, so a native build fails at the linker before any --help can run: "rust-lld: error: undefined symbol: drmModeCreateLease" and eleven more. Settled by hardware or QEMU, not by this generator. |
| `rivet-initd` | is PID 1 (cmd/rivet-initd/src/main.rs: fn main() -> !). It parses no arguments and its main never returns, confirmed by running --help under a SIGKILL timeout: the plain-SIGTERM form left it running past 180s because an init deliberately does not exit on a signal it was not written to handle. |
| `rivet-sysd` | no --help surface: refuses the flag by name with no usage text ("rivet-sysd: arguments: unknown argument \"--help\"", exit 1). Nothing to generate from. |
| `rivet-splash` | needs a framebuffer device to do anything: it ignores an unrecognised --help and then fails opening /dev/fb0, which only exists on a board. |
| `rivet-proxyd` | refuses before parsing any argument without RIVET_APP_DATA, which only the supervisor sets when it starts an installed application ("RIVET_APP_DATA is not set; this was not started by a Rivet"). No --help surface reachable off a running machine. |
| `rivet-dhcp-hook` | invoked by udhcpc's own calling convention (positional arguments and environment variables, not a --help surface); its refusal names that directly ("udhcpc said --help and set no interface"). |
| `rivet-dnsd` | no --help surface: takes exactly `--document PATH` and refuses anything else with a one-line usage ("REFUSED: usage: rivet-dnsd --document PATH", exit 1); it is started only by the supervisor, with that argument. |
